comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Root cause CONFIRMED at runtime (rebar-debug Phase 1), then fixed.

Discriminating experiment on a real store (epic + 3 children):
- baseline, all live:      signer == gate  (e3ff6fc064b016ea)
- CONTROL, one child DELETED: signer == gate (0fb0121a21cf9e9c) - both sides already filter 'deleted', which rules out 'the two enumerations diverge generally'
- TREATMENT, one child ARCHIVED: signer = 0fb0121a21cf9e9c (UNCHANGED - still counts it), gate = 1ffdcb3d79bd745a (dropped it) -> NOT EQUAL

snapshot.child_ids still contained the archived child. Exactly the predicted-if-true outcome.

FIX: a single shared predicate relation_snapshot.counts_as_plan_material_child (live only: excludes archived + deleted). The gate now enumerates WIDE (include_archived=True) and narrows through that one helper, so the two sides cannot diverge by construction. AC1 satisfied structurally.

IMPORTANT - AC1 and AC3 as written are MUTUALLY UNSATISFIABLE. AC3 asks that archiving a child leave the container's material fingerprint unchanged. But once archived children are excluded from the basis (AC1's 'live only'), archiving one necessarily removes it from the basis and so necessarily MOVES the fingerprint. The ticket's rationale had this inverted: it is the *include-archived* option that would leave the fingerprint untouched, not the exclude option that was chosen.

Resolved in favour of AC1 (the structural, primary criterion). The regression test now pins the invariant that actually cures the bug - signer and gate agree before AND after the archive - and explicitly records the accepted residual cost: archiving a child invalidates the container's attestation and requires a fresh review. That is recoverable, unlike the permanent unclaimable loop this bug caused. AC3 should be amended.

Verification: RED->GREEN with the test held out from the implementing agent; defect-seeded mutation (helper reverted to status != 'deleted') returns both tests to RED. The reporter's exact loop (epic + archived child -> review-plan -> claim) is now a permanent regression test in tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_plan_review_gate.py and reproduces the original failure when the fix is reverted.

comments.body: Phase 2 complete, pushed as Gerrit 1175 (Change-Id I4e73f709). RED->GREEN with mutation check. RED oracle: tests/unit/test_plan_relation_snapshot.py::test_signer_and_gate_material_agree_across_archive - baseline (all live) signer==gate, then archiving a child made signer keep it (9f28...) while gate dropped it (448e...) -> RED for the exact mechanism. GREEN via one shared predicate counts_as_plan_material_child (live only: excludes archived+deleted) plus a live_material_children gate helper that enumerates WIDE (include_archived=True) and narrows through it, so signer and gate cannot drift (AC1). Second test test_archived_child_excluded_from_child_ids_and_pins pins AC5 (archived child drops from child_ids AND plan-material-pins). Mutation note: reverting ONLY the shared helper makes both sides wrong SYMMETRICALLY (agreement test still passes), but the exclusion test catches it - the two tests are complementary, covering both divergence and symmetric-inclusion regressions. Actual files changed: relation_snapshot.py, attest.py, test_plan_relation_snapshot.py (NOT generation.py - it derives from snapshot.child_ids, fixed at source; NOT test_plan_material_pins.py - existing pin coverage stayed green). attest.py held at exactly 800 LOC (net-zero gate change via the shared helper + existing line-40 import). Gates: 29 unit + 94 plan-review lifecycle gate tests, lint, typecheck all green.

compiled_state.description:
Reported by a rebar client (report archived at `~/rebar-archived-child-claim-bug.md` on the
operator host) against `nava-rebar 0.10.1` (source build at `f0cf30a0e` + `bcb735630`) with
`verify.require_plan_review_for_claim = true`. **The divergence is reproduced in current
`main`**, so this is not fixed by upgrading.

## Symptom

When a container ticket has a child whose status is `archived`, `rebar review-plan <container>`
signs a material fingerprint computed over a child set that **includes** the archived child,
while the claim gate recomputes the fingerprint over a child set that **excludes** it. The two
can never agree, so every `review-plan` → `claim` sequence fails with:

```
Error: cannot start work on <id>: the plan was materially edited since review
(description/AC/file_impact/children changed).
```

Re-running `review-plan` cannot break the loop: each new attestation re-signs the same
larger basis the gate will again recompute smaller. The recovery the error itself prints
("run the plan review to earn an attestation, then start work") is non-terminating for this
ticket shape.

## Impact

Any container that has ever had a child archived — a normal board outcome when a child is
superseded or found to be a duplicate — becomes permanently unclaimable through the supported
path. The only exits are `claim --force` (which discards the very gate the config exists to
enforce) or mutating the board to detach/unarchive the child. The message is also actively
misleading: it reports a plan edit that did not happen, sending the operator to hunt a phantom
description change.

## Reproduction

1. Create an epic with N children, each with a `file_impact`.
2. Archive one child. It keeps `parent_id=<epic>`, gains `status=archived`.
3. `rebar review-plan <epic>` → `PASS`, signed.
4. `rebar claim <epic>` → fails with "the plan was materially edited since review".
5. Repeat 3–4 any number of times; identical failure, no edit in between.

## Reporter's evidence (measured, not inferred)

Epic `5bb5-2a98-b054-4d66` in the reporter's store: 12 live children plus archived child
`fb45-e43c-f0cb-4f5d` (`parent_id=5bb5-2a98-b054-4d66`, `status=archived`). Both fingerprints
were reproduced by re-implementing the basis from `material_fingerprint`:

| child set | fingerprint | computed by |
|---|---|---|
| 13 ids (incl. `fb45`) | `084b676f66849bab` | value embedded in the signed attestation |
| 12 ids (excl. `fb45`) | `236d5fa9f6944e87` | `attest.current_material_fingerprint()` at claim time |

- `rebar._reads.list_tickets(parent=<epic>)` returns 12 deterministically (three separate
  processes); `fb45` is absent.
- The stored attestation's `material:` manifest line is `084b676f66849bab`.
- The epic's *original* attestation (signed earlier, by a different operator) carries 13
  `plan-material-pin: child …` lines including `fb45-e43c-f0cb-4f5d` — the review side has been
  enumerating the archived child **consistently**, not intermittently.

## Root cause (confirmed in this checkout, current `main`)

The reporter narrowed the divergence to "somewhere below `list_tickets`" and named a relation
snapshot as a likely candidate. That is correct — the two sides do not in fact share an
enumeration:

- **Gate side** — `attest.current_material_fingerprint()`
  (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest.py:771`) calls
  `_reads.list_tickets(parent=canonical)`, whose default is `include_archived=False`
  (`src/rebar/_reads.py:87`) → **archived children excluded**.
- **Signer side** — the signed generation's `own_material` is computed in
  `generation.from_snapshot()` (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/generation.py:84`) from
  `snapshot.child_ids`, which `collect_plan_relation_snapshot()` builds by scanning reduced
  states and admitting every candidate whose parent resolves to the subject and whose
  `status != "deleted"` (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/relation_snapshot.py:283`) → **archived
  children included**.

So the divergence is the archived-vs-deleted predicate: the snapshot filters only `deleted`,
while `list_tickets` filters `archived` too. `current_material_fingerprint`'s docstring claims
it is "matching `orchestrator.material_fingerprint`" — that stated invariant is what is broken,
and nothing enforces it because the child predicate is spelled independently at each site.

## Fix direction

Exclude non-live children (archived, deleted) from the material basis, and apply that policy in
**one shared helper both the signer and the gate call** rather than independently at two sites.
Material is meant to capture *the plan*, and an archived child is no longer part of the plan;
this is also what the gate already does, so the gate becomes correct by definition and only the
signer changes.

Deliberately **not** choosing the symmetric alternative (include archived on both sides): that
would make archiving a child a *material edit*, invalidating a parent's attestation for a board
action that changed no plan content — trading this bug for a subtler one. The reporter reached
the same conclusion independently.

Note `relation_snapshot.child_ids` also feeds `related_material` and the per-child
`plan-material-pin` manifest lines, so the change must keep those consistent with the new basis
(archived children should stop being pinned), and existing attestations that pin an archived
child must not be treated as forgeries — only as stale in the ordinary way.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A single shared helper defines "children that count as plan material" (live only: excludes
   `archived` and `deleted`), and both `generation.from_snapshot()`/`collect_plan_relation_snapshot()`
   and `attest.current_material_fingerprint()` obtain their child set through it — no
   independently spelled status predicate remains at either site.
2. Regression test: archive a child of a container, then `review-plan` → `claim` succeeds.
   Currently fails.
3. ~~Regression test: archiving a child alone does **not** invalidate a container's existing
   valid attestation (material fingerprint unchanged across the archive).~~
   **AMENDED — the original AC3 was unsatisfiable together with AC1.** Once archived children
   are excluded from the material basis (AC1's "live only"), archiving a child necessarily
   removes it from that basis and so necessarily MOVES the fingerprint. The rationale above had
   this inverted: it is the *include-archived-on-both-sides* option that would leave the
   fingerprint untouched, not the exclude option that was chosen. Replacement AC3:

   **Regression test: the signer-side and gate-side fingerprints agree BOTH before and after a
   child is archived.** That is the invariant that actually cures the bug. The accepted residual
   cost is explicit: archiving a child invalidates the container's attestation and requires a
   fresh `review-plan`. That is recoverable, unlike the permanent unclaimable loop this bug
   caused, and it is the price of keeping "material" mean "the live plan".
4. Regression test asserting the docstring invariant directly: for a container with a mix of
   live, archived, and deleted children, the signer-side fingerprint and
   `current_material_fingerprint()` are equal.
5. `plan-material-pin` manifest lines for the container no longer include archived children,
   and an attestation signed *before* the fix (pinning an archived child) is handled as stale /
   re-reviewable, not as a signature failure.
6. Full suite, `make lint`, and `make typecheck` green.

## Workarounds until fixed

- Detach the archived child from the parent (`rebar edit <child> --parent=null`) so both sides
  enumerate the same set, then re-run `review-plan` and `claim`. The reporter applied this to
  `fb45-e43c-f0cb-4f5d`, which is now unparented in their store.
- `rebar claim <id> --force="<reason>"` works but discards the gate.

file_impact.reason: signer-side child_ids filters only deleted (line 283) — must exclude archived via the shared helper
from_snapshot computes signed own_material from snapshot.child_ids
gate-side current_material_fingerprint must call the same shared helper; its docstring states the broken invariant
regression: archived child excluded from child_ids / material basis
regression: archived child no longer pinned; pre-fix attestation is stale, not a forgery

compiled_state.title: Archived child permanently blocks claim on its parent: signer includes it in the material basis, claim gate excludes it
